summary: LLM inference costs can be reduced dramatically through layered optimization strategies without sacrificing output quality. Research from 2026 shows that combining prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, and output constraints can cut API spend by 50–80%, with PwC research across 500 agent sessions finding prompt caching alone reduces costs by 41–80%. Developers spending thousands per month on flagship models can typically reach equivalent performance at a fraction of the cost by applying even a subset of these techniques.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors for repeated prompt prefixes on the provider side. When the same static prefix (e.g., a large system prompt or knowledge base) is sent again, the provider skips recomputing it and charges a heavily discounted cache-hit rate — up to 90% less on input tokens. Every major provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) now supports this natively.
techniques.example: Place your 20,000-token RAG knowledge base or detailed system prompt at the very top of every request, before any dynamic user content. Anthropic activates caching automatically for prefixes over 1,024 tokens (Haiku) or 2,048 tokens (Sonnet/Opus), dropping cached token cost by 90%.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Intercepts incoming requests and computes an embedding of the query. If a semantically similar query was answered recently, the cached response is returned immediately — no LLM call is made at all. This is distinct from prompt caching: it eliminates entire API round-trips for near-duplicate questions rather than discounting repeated prefixes.
techniques.savings: 40–60% reduction in total API calls (45% cache hit rate reported in production)
techniques.example: Deploy GPTCache or a Redis semantic cache in front of a customer support bot. When a user asks 'What is your return policy?' and a similar question was answered 10 minutes ago, the cached answer is returned in milliseconds with zero token spend.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Classifies each incoming request by complexity and routes it to the cheapest model that can handle it adequately. Simple classification or extraction tasks go to budget-tier models; only complex reasoning or high-stakes outputs reach frontier models. This exploits the 10–50x price differential between model tiers.
techniques.savings: 60–80% reduction in average cost per request
techniques.example: Route classify and extract tasks to GPT-3.5 or Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5 per million tokens), summarization to GPT-4o-mini or Sonnet 4.6 ($3/$15), and only complex multi-step reasoning to GPT-4 or Opus 4.8 ($5/$25). A reported production split of 70% budget / 25% mid-tier / 5% frontier cuts average cost by ~75%.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Rewrites or truncates prompts to remove redundant phrasing, filler words, over-specified instructions, and excessive few-shot examples before sending to the API. Shorter prompts reduce input token counts directly and also speed up prefill time.
techniques.example: Cut your system prompt from 800 tokens to under 200 by replacing verbose format instructions with a single JSON schema example and removing filler phrases like 'Please make sure to…'. A 30% prompt length reduction translates directly to a 30% reduction in input costs.

techniques.name: Output Constraints (max_tokens + structured output)
techniques.description: Set explicit max_tokens limits on every API call and use structured output schemas (JSON mode, function calling) instead of free-form prose. Output tokens cost 4–5x more than input tokens on flagship models, so preventing runaway responses and eliminating verbose formatting instructions has outsized impact.
techniques.example: Add max_tokens: 300 to every customer support API call and switch the response format to a JSON schema with fields like {answer, confidence, escalate}. This eliminated verbose prose wrapping and cut average output tokens by 50% in reported production deployments.

techniques.name: Batch API Processing
techniques.description: Instead of sending requests one at a time, queue non-urgent requests and submit them as a batch job. Providers like Anthropic and OpenAI offer 50% discounts on batch API calls that tolerate up to 24-hour latency, making it ideal for offline workflows like document processing, classification pipelines, or nightly report generation.
techniques.example: Run nightly document summarization or dataset labeling jobs through Anthropic's Batch API instead of real-time calls. Combined with prompt caching, Anthropic's own documentation shows up to 95% total cost reduction for large, repetitive workloads.

techniques.name: RAG Optimization and Reranking
techniques.description: Instead of stuffing an entire knowledge base into every prompt, retrieve only the top-k most relevant chunks using embeddings, then apply a reranker to trim to the fewest tokens that still answer the query. Fewer retrieved tokens means shorter prompts and lower costs, especially when combined with prompt caching on the static system prompt.
techniques.savings: 20–50% reduction in input tokens for RAG pipelines
techniques.example: Replace a 15,000-token full-document context with a reranker (e.g., Cohere Rerank or a cross-encoder) that selects the 3 most relevant 500-token chunks. This cuts RAG input tokens by ~80% while maintaining answer quality for most queries.

techniques.name: Quantized and Smaller Open-Weight Models (Self-Hosting)
techniques.description: For high-volume or latency-sensitive workloads, run quantized open-weight models locally or on owned infrastructure. Models like Gemma 4 26B A4B, Qwen variants, or DeepSeek R1 distills run efficiently on consumer hardware and eliminate per-token API fees entirely after infrastructure cost.
techniques.savings: 70–95% reduction in marginal per-request cost at sufficient scale
techniques.example: Serve Gemma 4 26B A4B via vLLM on a machine with 32–64 GB unified memory for internal tooling that handles 500,000 requests/month. The per-token marginal cost drops to near zero, with payback vs. OpenAI API fees typically under 2 months at that volume.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library for LLM APIs. Intercepts requests, embeds queries, and returns cached responses for semantically similar questions. Supports multiple vector stores and embedding models.

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Redis-native semantic caching layer using vector similarity search. Integrates with LangChain and LlamaIndex to cache LLM responses by semantic similarity, eliminating redundant API calls at scale.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis Cloud free tier available; paid plans from $7/month

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified Python SDK and proxy that normalizes 100+ LLM provider APIs into one interface, enabling model routing, fallbacks, load balancing, cost tracking, and budget enforcement across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and open-source models.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and cost optimization platform. Provides request logging, cost analytics, prompt caching insights, rate limiting, and a caching proxy layer. Works via a one-line proxy URL change for OpenAI and Anthropic.
tools.pricing_paid: Free up to 10,000 requests/month; paid from $20/month

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: Popular LLM application framework with built-in caching backends (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, GPTCache), prompt templates for compression, and model routing abstractions. Widely used to wire together RAG pipelines with cost-aware retrieval.

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: Production-grade LLM gateway that pairs semantic caching with provider-native prompt caching for best-in-class combined savings. Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers with a unified API and observability dashboard.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering unified API access to 250+ LLMs with built-in semantic caching, automatic retries, model fallbacks, prompt management, and detailed cost analytics. Designed for production reliability and cost control.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference server for self-hosted LLMs. Implements PagedAttention for efficient GPU memory use, continuous batching, and quantization support. The standard choice for serving open-weight models behind an API endpoint.

tools.name: Maxim AI
tools.description: LLM cost and quality optimization platform covering prompt caching analysis, model routing recommendations, and production monitoring. Highlights the highest-leverage cost levers for each workload type.

quick_wins: Enable provider-native prompt caching immediately: restructure prompts so all static content (system prompt, knowledge base, instructions) comes first and never changes between requests — Anthropic and OpenAI apply 75–90% discounts on cached prefixes with zero code changes beyond prompt ordering.

Set max_tokens on every API call and switch to structured JSON output: output tokens cost 4–5x more than input tokens, and unconstrained responses are the single fastest way to overspend — capping output and using schemas typically cuts output costs by 30–50% with one parameter change.

Trim system prompts to under 200 tokens: audit your system prompts and remove filler phrases, redundant instructions, and over-specified formatting rules — a 30% prompt length reduction translates directly to a 30% input cost reduction across every single API call.

Route simple tasks to budget-tier models: identify your highest-volume, lowest-complexity calls (classification, extraction, yes/no decisions) and switch them to GPT-3.5, Claude Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5 per million tokens), or Gemini Flash — budget models cost 10–50x less than frontier models for tasks they handle equally well.

Submit non-real-time workloads via Batch API: any offline task — nightly summaries, document processing, dataset labeling, bulk classification — qualifies for OpenAI or Anthropic's 50% batch discount with no quality trade-off, requiring only a minor workflow change to queue and poll results.
